messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Devon Reyes <devon@brighthealthai.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: Inference scale conversation — GPU isolation & burst requirements

Hi Devon —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap so we have the pain/goals captured and clear next steps. Really appreciated the context on where BrightHealth AI is now and what success looks like.

Summary of what I heard (please correct any mistakes):
- Primary pain: unpredictable per-request latency under peak and noisy multi-tenant interference when PHI workloads run (you need physical or strong logical isolation).
- Current stack: prototype uses a mix of open transformer models deployed in-house (PyTorch + custom KV cache layer). Production traffic currently on GKE with GPU node pools.
- Traffic profile: baseline ~200 inference TPS for anonymized routing logic; peak behavior up to ~900 TPS for short daily windows (90–120s bursts), sustained peaks of ~400 TPS for ~30–45 minutes.
- Success criteria for pilot: predictable 95th-percentile token latency <150ms, no cross-tenant noisy-neighbor incidents, quota isolation for PHI workloads, and measurable cost per request that is <= 50% of your current self-hosted spend per token.
- Operational asks: SOC 2 evidence, ability to pin model versions, and audit logs for per-request routing.

Potential Redwood fit (high level):
- Dedicated GPU pool (reserved) for predictable throughput and isolation; optional burst policy that allows autoscaling up to N extra GPUs for short windows to cover the 900 TPS spikes.
- Prefix/KV caching and request routing to reduce tail tokens during burst windows.
- Integration points: VPC peering and customer-managed KMS for keys.

Requested next steps we discussed:
1) Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra/ML engineer + our serving runtime lead to walk through workload traces and sizing assumptions (suggested window: Feb 21–22).
2) You to share the traffic-estimates.csv (attached) and any model sequence-length distributions.
3) Redwood to return a pilot proposal: 4-week reserved pool recommendation (GPU type + count), burst policy design, and a preliminary pilot SOW.
4) Procurement: we’ll prepare a draft SOW and NDAs (DocuSign link to follow) and connect with your procurement contact.

Attachments: traffic-estimates.csv (uploaded), initial notes.

If that aligns, I’ll book the deep-dive and loop in Karhik (pricing) and Dylan (deployment lead).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Thanks for the tidy recap, that matches our internal takeaways. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The 900 TPS spikes are very bursty and often driven by batch events (insurance-window processing). Spikes are typically 60–180s; we need a burst policy that can ramp quickly and then scale down with minimal cost overhead.
- PHI requirement: isolation must be demonstrable; logical multi-tenant separation is acceptable if we can show dedicated device allocation for PHI model runs and end-to-end encryption.
- Security: please include SOC 2 Type II evidence and an outline of audit log retention (we need 6+ months).

Procurement asked that the pilot quote include a line-item for a 4-week reserved pool and a separate line for burst (pay-as-you-go for extra GPUs during windows). Also, can you provide an estimate of how much KV/prefix caching will reduce token processing cost under our peak patterns?

Happy to do Feb 21 for the deep-dive (morning CT). I’ll forward the traffic CSV and a short sequence-length export later today.

-Devon

CTO, BrightHealth AI
